title: Fleet lanes never consume a batch — wave seeder hands each lane b[0] only, so 'prefer a whole batch as top_n' is dead guidance under fleet scope
console_claim: 2026-07-28 operator prioritized; being fixed console-first this session (batch-14 wave-1 in flight); do not seed into a lane
evidence: Live wave-1 of batch-14 (cycles 1127/1128): both lane-scope.json files carry a SINGLE-element todo_ids despite the schema being []string, and cycle-1127's triage rationale states verbatim 'fleet_scope restricts this cycle to the single assigned todo-id verdict-coherence-auditor-vs-egps; no other candidates were considered' — while the SAME cycle's triage prompt renders 'prefer selecting a whole batch as top_n (its items share a worktree, build, and audit — one cycle amortizes the pipeline across them)'. Root: SelectFleetWidthTopN (topn_width.go:66-67) partitions the backlog into file-disjoint buckets then keeps ONLY b[0] per bucket as the lane representative, discarding bucket-mates; the batch-consumption intent can therefore only ever engage in single-lane (non-fleet) runs.
notes: fleet.Partition's buckets are already the right within-lane batches: members land in one bucket BECAUSE they share files (same area, one worktree amortizes them) and buckets are mutually file-disjoint (cross-lane safe). Fix shape: seed each lane with a capped prefix of its bucket (cap matching the 4-item batch chunk size / triage size bands) instead of b[0] alone — lane-scope.TodoIDs already supports it. Lane scope then becomes a MENU, not a pin: triage keeps authority to commit a subset as top_n and defer the rest (today's semantics treat the single id as mandatory). Preserve the cycle-640 lane-identity invariant: scout and triage must see the SAME scope set, materialized before any phase. Sequence AFTER inboxbatch-cross-campaign-fusion: with fusion unfixed, a mega-cluster bucket could hand a lane 4 unrelated items and recreate the bag-cycle problem the area floor just killed.
acceptance: RED first: SelectFleetWidthTopN (or its successor seam) returns each lane's bucket members up to the cap, not just b[0]; existing single-focus (count<2) behavior unchanged.
A fleet wave's lane-scope.json carries >1 todo_ids when the backlog has clusterable same-area items, and the two lanes' id sets remain file-disjoint.
Triage inside a multi-id lane may commit a subset and defer the rest without a scope-violation warning.
